title: The world is a big tangle
takeaway: One day you'll have to leave this world, so don't get too tangled up in it.
scene: This ghazal is printed in two columns, and each row is one couplet. The poet's hopes have collapsed, and he thinks about how short and messy life in this world is.

original: میری آساں دا مندر ڈھہ گیا اے
تیری دنیا چھڈ جانا پے گیا اے
transliteration: Meri aasaan da mandar dheh gaya ae
Teri duniya chhad jaana pai gaya ae
translation: The temple of my hopes has collapsed;
now I have to leave this world of yours.
couplets.story: Everything he hoped for has fallen down like an old building. Now it's time for him to leave this world.

original: کدی دوری کدی یاداں دا خنجر
دل کملے دے اندر لہہ گیا اے
transliteration: Kadi doori, kadi yaadaan da khanjar
Dil kamle de andar leh gaya ae
translation: Sometimes distance, sometimes the dagger of memories
has sunk into my foolish heart.
couplets.story: Being far away hurts. Remembering hurts too, like a knife going into his silly heart.

original: کرنا ہور کیہ طوفانی مینہ نے
اکو کوٹھا سی اوہ وی بہہ گیا اے
transliteration: Karna hor ki toofaani meenh ne
Ikko kotha si, oh vi beh gaya ae
translation: What more could the storm's rain do?
I had only one little house, and even that has collapsed.
couplets.story: The storm can't do anything worse now. He only had one small mud house, and the rain has already brought it down.

original: ستی سدھراں نوں اوہنے آ جگایا
کاں گوکن بنیرے بہہ گیا اے
transliteration: Sutti sadhraan nu ohne aa jagaaya
Kaan gookan banere beh gaya ae
translation: My sleeping longings were woken up
by a crow that came and sat cawing on the roof.
couplets.story: In Punjabi villages, a crow cawing on your roof means a guest or a loved one is coming. When he heard the crow, all his old hopes woke up again.

original: گلی نوں تاہنگ سی اک آہلنے دی
مری تے مونہہ چہ تیلا رہ گیا اے
transliteration: Gali nu taangh si ik aahlne di
Mari te moonh ch teela reh gaya ae
translation: The little bird longed for a nest;
it died with a twig still in its beak.
couplets.story: A little bird wanted to build a nest. It died before finishing, still holding a twig in its beak. That's how he feels: his dreams ended halfway through.

original: وفا الفت محبت نوں بھلا کے
بندہ اپنی حدوں لہہ گیا اے
transliteration: Vafa ulfat mohabbat nu bhula ke
Banda apni haddon leh gaya ae
translation: people have gone beyond their limits.
couplets.story: People have forgotten how to be loyal and loving. They've crossed lines they shouldn't cross.

original: گوا کے انکھ تے اپنی انا نوں
بندہ بندے دے پیریں پے گیا اے
transliteration: Gava ke ankh te apni ana nu
Banda bande de paireen pai gaya ae
translation: Losing their self-respect and their dignity,
people have fallen at other people's feet.
couplets.story: People have thrown away their self-respect and are bowing down to other people, as if humans were their masters.

original: عشق وچ دل بڑا سی جی دار میرا
ایہہ ہاواں ہوکے ہاڑے سب سہہ گیا اے
transliteration: Ishq vich dil bara si jee-daar mera
Eh haavaan hauke haare sab seh gaya ae
translation: In love, my heart was very brave:
it bore all these sighs, sobs and pleas.
couplets.story: His heart was brave in love. It took every sigh and tear and kept going.

original: بڑا جنجال اے دنیا دا احمدؔ
فقیر بے نوا کیہ کہہ گیا اے
transliteration: Bara janjaal ae duniya da Ahmad
Faqeer be-nawa ki keh gaya ae
translation: Ahmad, this world is a great tangle:
that's what the penniless faqir said as he passed.
couplets.story: He ends with what a poor holy man once said: this world is a giant tangle. Don't get caught in it.

deeper: The last couplet holds the poem's lesson. The world is a 'janjaal', a mess of strings that catches you, and the faqir who owns nothing sees it most clearly. 'People have fallen at other people's feet' laments the loss of dignity that comes from bowing to anyone but God. The poem starts with 'I have to leave this world' and ends with a holy man's warning not to get tangled in it. This life is a short stay, not a home.
why: The little bird that died holding a twig is one of the most touching images in the book.
prompt: What's something in your life that feels like a 'tangle'? What would it take to step back from it?
notes: Printed in two columns; each row is read as one couplet.
